<h3 id="the-work-the-erp-never-sees"><strong>The work the ERP never sees</strong></h3>
<p>SAP runs most of the world's largest companies. The majority still run it on-premise, customized over twenty years, and that whole ecosystem got skipped by the AI wave.</p>
<p>Here is what that looks like on the ground. The real work of procurement and planning happens where the ERP cannot see it: inboxes, spreadsheets, and phone calls. A buyer opens 47 unread supplier emails, reads quotes in five incompatible formats, re-types the numbers into Excel, builds the comparison by hand, chases delivery dates, and finally records the outcome in SAP. Hours per request, every day. We interviewed 200 companies and shadowed procurement & SAP teams for weeks watching this happen. Nobody was exaggerating.</p>
<h3 id="what-the-ai-employees-do"><strong>What the AI employees do</strong></h3>
<p>SpaceFlow agents do that work end to end and stage every action for a human to approve:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Sourcing.</strong> A purchase request comes in. The agent qualifies it, picks suppliers from the company's own purchase history, and sends the RFQs. Supplier replies land as messy human emails; the agent reads them the way a buyer does and extracts price, lead time, and minimum order. It compares bids, flags risk (a supplier that shipped late three times last quarter), and sends the counter-offer. The buyer sees one card with a recommendation and a confidence score. One click approves it.</li>
<li><strong>Planning.</strong> The agents keep supply plans in line with real demand and prepare the orders and the numbers behind every planning meeting, daily instead of once a month.</li>
<li><strong>Spend control.</strong> They match invoices against contracts and catch price drift and off-contract buying before it compounds.</li>
</ul>
<p>Humans stay in control. Every agent has per-action autonomy limits; everything above a threshold waits in an approval queue, and every step is logged and auditable. The ERP stays the system of record, SAP or otherwise. Every feature in the product is exposed over MCP as well as REST, so the whole system is agent-operable by design.</p>
<h3 id="what-it-is-worth"><strong>What it is worth</strong></h3>
<p>Work that takes a buyer hours happens in minutes. Across our customers: 3x faster RFQ cycles, $120K saved per year at one company, off-contract spending cut 42% at another, and one customer canceled three planned hires it no longer needed. A shared company brain learns how each company buys and decides, so the agents get better with every cycle.</p>
<h3 id="why-on-premise-and-what-we-had-to-build-for-it"><strong>Why on-premise, and what we had to build for it</strong></h3>
<p>The largest enterprises keep SAP in their own datacenters because their data cannot leave. The same rule kept AI out: they will never send twenty years of operating history to someone else's cloud.</p>
<p>So we bring the models to the data. SpaceFlow is a managed runtime for enterprise AI agents: we operate the models, the agents, and the compute wherever the customer's data must live. Our cloud, their private cloud, or their own hardware inside their own walls. Same product in every deployment; data never leaves the perimeter. No migration, nothing to rip out, live in days.</p>
<h3 id="the-deeper-bet-enterprise-work-that-can-be-checked"><strong>The deeper bet: enterprise work that can be checked</strong></h3>
<p>AI got good at code because every answer could be checked. SpaceFlow brings the same loop to enterprise work. Each time a person approves or corrects a task, that verdict is saved, and the verdicts become evals, the tests the AI is measured against. The AI improves at each company's specific way of working, and finance sees exactly what it did and what it saved. Our bet is that enterprise AI becomes real when its work can be checked.</p>
<h3 id="where-we-are"><strong>Where we are</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>$400M in annual supplier spend runs through the product, and it is growing.</li>
<li>Our first enterprise contract is signed with a national restaurant brand. That customer's Chief Supply Chain Officer went on to invest personally upon seeing Spaceflow’s capabilities.</li>
<li>Before YC, we built an autonomous procurement engine with a medical manufacturer and saw both gaps firsthand: the work lives outside the ERP, and nobody could tell whether the AI did it right.</li>
</ul>
